content_voiceover: Continuing with the INO-VATE data, inotuzumab also translated into better bridging to transplant and modest survival benefit. Seventy eight percent of patients achieved MRD negativity with inotuzumab compared to twenty eight percent with standard of care. This deeper remission allowed more patients to proceed to subsequent hematopoietic stem cell transplant, forty one percent overall with inotuzumab versus only eleven percent with standard therapy. Even among patients who achieved CR or CRi, transplant rates trended higher with inotuzumab. Looking at survival curves, median overall survival was seven point seven months with inotuzumab versus six point seven months with standard of care, a hazard ratio of zero point seven seven that was of borderline statistical significance. However, progression free survival showed a much clearer benefit, five months versus one point eight months, with a hazard ratio of zero point four five and a highly significant p value. So the take home message is that inotuzumab dramatically improves response rate, MRD negativity, and progression free survival, and enables more transplants, though the overall survival benefit was modest, likely because many standard of care patients who failed treatment crossed over to receive other salvage therapies.
keypoints: MRD negativity seventy eight percent with inotuzumab versus twenty eight percent with standard of care
Subsequent HSCT rate forty one percent with inotuzumab versus eleven percent with standard of care
Median OS seven point seven versus six point seven months, hazard ratio zero point seven seven, p equals zero point zero four
Median PFS five versus one point eight months, hazard ratio zero point four five, p less than zero point zero zero one
keypoint_voiceover: Key numbers to memorize from INO-VATE. Inotuzumab nearly tripled MRD negativity and quadrupled the rate of bridging to transplant. Progression free survival benefit was robust and highly significant, while the overall survival benefit was smaller and only borderline significant, an important nuance for board questions.
